full_judgment:
Sheikh Hassan Arif J: Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order being No. 59 dated 24-11-2011 (Annexure-D-2) passed by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Jessore in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 11 of 2007 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

2. Short back ground facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, are that Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Benapole Branch, Police Station-Benapole, District-Jessore-(respondentNo.3), as plaintiff, filed Artha Rin Suit No. 31 of 2006 before the First Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore against the petitioner and others for realization of loan of Taka 1,24,84,730. The defendants having not contested, the said suit was decreed ex-parte on 22-2-2007 (decree drawn up on 1-3-2007). Accordingly, the respondent-bank put the said decree into execution through Artha Execution Case No. 11 of 2007 filed before the same Adalat. In the said execution process, the mortgaged properties of the petitioner and others were put on auction-sale through news papers in view of the provisions under section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("the said Ain"). However, the said auction did not succeed due to the absence of bidders. The executing Adalat then proceeded for the 2nd auction in view of the provisions under sub-section (4) of section 33 of the said Ain and fixed 5-11-2007 for the same. The 2nd auction also ended up in failure as no bidder participated therein. In such situation, the decree holder bank, on 7-3-2011, filed an application before the executing Adalat praying for title of the mortgaged property in view of the provisions under sub-section (7) of section 33, whereupon the petitioner filed objection against' the same. After hearing the parties, the Adalat, vide impugned order dated 24-11-2011, allowed the application filed by the bank conferring title of the mortgaged properties upon it and fixed 28-11-2011 for presentation and preparation of certificate of sale. At this stage, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid Rule. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this Court, by order dated 15-12-2011, stayed operation of the impugned order dated 24-11-2011.

3. The Rule is contested by the respondent No. 3 bank through learned advocates, who also filed affidavit-in-opposition.

4. Mr Shah Mohd Monir Sharif, learned advocate, along with Mr Mohammad Imran Jahangir, learned advocate, appearing for the petitioner, mainly submits that since the Adalat proceeded for the 2nd auction under sub-section (4) of section 33 and completed the same unsuccessfully, the Adalat acted without jurisdiction in conferring title on the' decree-holder-bank under subsection (7) of section 33 of the said Ain. According to him, since 2nd auction took place, the decree holder batik as Well as the Adalat had no option but to proceed' for conferring the right of possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property on the decree-holder-bank in view of sub-section (5) of section 33. In short, Mr Sharif wants to convince this Court that once the 2ndauction is taken place in view of sub-section (4) of section 33, there is no scope either for the Adalat or for the decree holder to go for the conferment of title of the mortgaged property in view of sub-section (7) of section 33 of the said Ain.

5. Mr Sharnim Khaled Ahmed, learned senior counsel, along with Mr Mohammed Abdul Baset, learned advocate, appearing for the respondent No. 3-bank, on the other hand, submits that the provisions under section 33 have given free leverages to the decree holder either to go for the 2nd auction or to seek conferment of title upon it under sub-section(7) of section 33 of the said Ain. According to him, even if the 2nd auction is taken place, the decree holder will at any stage be at liberty to ask for conferment of title in view of the provisions under sub-section (7) of section 33. Mr Ahmed further argues that since sub-section (7) of section 33 commences with the words "notwithstanding anything contained in sub-sections (4) and (5)", the provisions under sub-sections (4) and (5) have been made subjugated to the provisions under sub-section (7). In other words, according to him, the provisions under, sub-section (7), in clear terms, have ruled out the applicability of the provisions under sub-section (4) and (5) and, as such, even if the proceedings under sub-sections (4) and (5) are adopted or initiated, the decree holder can exercise its option to apply for title under sub-section (7) even in the middle stage of the proceedings under sub-sections (4) and (5). 6. The main question to be determined in this writ petition is whether once the 2 auction sale in view of sub-section (4) of section 33 is adopted, in other words, if the 2nd auction is taken place unsuccessfully, whether or not the bank can apply for the conferment of title of the mortgaged property in view of the provisions under sub-section (7) of section 33, and, upon such application, whether the Adalat can confer such tile under the said provisions.

7. It appears that, in view of sub-sections (1),( 2), (2Ka), (2Kha), (2Ga) and (3) of section 33 of the said Ain, the Adalat is obliged to go for an auction sale of the mortgaged property, and the holding of such 11 auction of the mortgaged property is mandatory. The said 11 auction has to be taken place in accordance with the provisions and procedures mentioned in the above mentioned sub-sections of section 33. Sub-section (4) of section 33 speaks about the 2nd auction after the 11 auction as taken place under the said sub-sections fails either for absence of bidders or for any other reasons. In going for the 2nd auction, the procedures mentioned as regards the 11 auction have to be followed. Sub-section (5) further provides that if the 2nd auction, as taken place in view of sub-section (4), fails for any reason, the right to possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property will be conferred on the decree holder and, in such case, the decree holder will be at liberty to realize the decreetal amount through sale of the mortgaged property, again in accordance with the pro-visions mentioned in sub-sections (1),( 2), (2Ka), (2Kha), (2Ga), (3) and (4) of section 33. Sub-section (6), however, provides that if excess money is realized through such auction sale, the decree-holder will refund the same to the judgment debtor, and if the sale proceeds do not cover the decreetal amount, the decree-holder will be at liberty to go for the 2nd or further execution cases in view of section 28 of the said Ain. Sub-section (6Ka) further provides that if the decree holder fails to sell the mortgaged property after such con-ferment of right to possession and enjoyment, it will be at liberty to go for further execution cases.

8. The above provisions under section 33 describe the chronology of actions to be taken by the decree-holder as well as the Adalat for realization of the decreetal amount through sale of the mortgaged property. However, sub-sections 6 (Kha) and (7) of section 33 have made a leap-frog approach in the said chronology of actions. According to sub-section 6(Kha), even after con-ferment of right to possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property, the decree-holder would be at liberty to apply for conferment of title of the mortgaged property on it under sub-section (7) for a period of 6(six) years, and this sub-section 6(Kha) even stars with a strong non-obstante pro-vision with the words (“"এই ধারার ভিন্নতর যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন"”)(notwithstanding anything contained in this section). This means, the Legislature has given this sub-section, namely sub-section 6(Kha), a special overriding status which is that whatever is contained in the entire section 33 of the said Ain, after conferment of the right to enjoyment and possession of the mortgaged property under sub-section (5), the decree holder would be at liberty to apply for the conferment of title during a period of 6(six) years and that the title of the said property would automatically vest in the decree holder and a certificate to that effect would be issued by the Adalat upon expiry of the said six years' period. It further appears that, the Legislature has given another powerful leverage on the decree holder under sub-section (7), which also starts with the words [“উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও”] [notwithstanding the provisions in sub-sections (4) and (5)1 According to the provisions under this sub-section (7), notwithstanding the provisions under sub-sections (4) and (5), the decree holder will be at liberty to apply for conferment of title of the mortgaged property on it, and once such application is made, the Adalat will refrain from following the proceedings under sub- sections (4) and (5) [উপ ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর কার্যক্রম অনুসরণ করা হইতে বিরত থাকিবে], and, accordingly, issue a certificate declaring that the title of the said property has been vested as such. Again, once such certificate is issued, the same will be regarded as a title deed and will be registered accordingly by the local sub-registrar.

<u>9. As indicated above, the Legislature has deliberately given sub-sections 6(Kha) and (7) a separate status. Thus, the provisions under sub-section 6(kha) are such that they can be followed even notwithstanding whatever contained in the entire section 33. This means, once the right to enjoyment and possession of the mortgaged property is conferred on the decree holder, it will be at liberty to even immediately apply for conferment of title under sub-section (7). In which case, it will not be obligatory on it to try to sell the property through 2nd, 3rd or 4th auctions. To obtain that special status under sub-section 6(kha), the precondition is that the right to possession and enjoyment of the property is conferred on the decree holder in view of sub-section (5).</u>

<u>10. Similarly, sub-section (7) has also given a special leverage on the decree holder; According to the said provisions, not-withstanding the provisions under sub-sections (4) and (5), the decree holder will be at liberty to file an application for conferment of title on it by the Adalat, and once such application is made, the Adalat will even refrain from following the proceedings under sub-sections (4) and (5) and will confer such title on the decree holder through a certificate of title issued by it declaring such title. The only hurdle in the said provisions under sub-section (7) is that the provisions under sub-sections (1), (2), 2(Ka), 2(Kha), 2(Ga) and (3) of section 33 cannot be jeopardized. In other words, it recognizes the mandatory nature of the 1st auction in view of sub-sections (1), (2), 2(Ka), 2(Kha), 2(Ga) and (3). Thus, once the 1st auction is done and it fails for any reason, the decree-holder bank will be at liberty to either proceed for the 2nd auction and then for conferment of right to possession and enjoyment under sub-section (5) or it can ask for conferment of tile under sub-section (7). This option of conferment of title can be exercised by the decree holder either immediately after the 1st auction or after conferment of right to possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property or even after conclusion of the 2 auction, though unsuccessfully. This intention of the Legislature to give almost a free leverage to the decree holder is clear from the provisions mentioned under sub-section 6(Kha) and section (7) of section 33. While sub-section 6(Kha) has given the decree holder a free leverage to apply for title once the right to enjoyment and possession of the mortgaged property is conferred on it under sub-section (5), sub-section (7) gives it another leverage by providing that notwithstanding the provisions under sub-section (4) and(5), the decree holder will be at liberty to apply for conferment of title. The only precondition is to satisfy the Court that the 1st auction has taken place. In. the course of hearing, we have examined the earlier decisions of this Court in Setara Begum vs Al-Arafa Islami Bank, 14 MLR 480 = 61 DLR 791 and Atiqullah vs Artha Rin Adalat, 16 BLC 486, as referred to by the parties. However, since those decisions did not address the issues as raised in this writ petition directly, we do not need to discuss them with elaboration.</u>

<u>11. In the case before us, the admitted position is that the 200 auction has taken place, though not successfully as no bidder participated. This means, in the meantime, the mandatory precondition of holding the 1st auction has already been fulfilled. Thus, the decree holder bank is now at liberty to wait for the conferment of right to possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property under sub-section (5) and then apply for the conferment of title or wait for 6(six) years for such conferment of title automatically. At the same time, it has in the meantime acquired the other leverage to apply for the conferment of title directly even without waiting for the conferment of right-to enjoyment and possession of the mortgaged property under sub-section (5). This free leverage of decree holder bank is clear from the provisions under sub-section (7), which at first has overruled the effect of the provisions under sub-sections (4)  and (5) and then provides that once an application is made by the decree holder for, conferment of title, the Adalat will even refrain from following the proceedings under sub-sections (4) and (5). This means at any stage of the proceedings under sub-sections (4) and (5), the decree-holder-bank is entitled to apply for such conferment of title. Therefore, though argued by Mr Sharif, we do not find any indication in the clear provisions under section 33 that once the 2nd auction is taken place-the decree holder can only ask for conferment of right to possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property. We rather find that the provisions under sub-section (7) have made it clear that the Legislature wanted to give a free leverage to the decree holder bank or financial-institution to apply for the conferment of title at any stage after the 1st auction is done and failed. Therefore, just holding of the in auction will not be a bar against the decree-holder bank preventing it from applying to get the title of the mortgaged property under sub-section (7).</u>

12. Regard being had to the above discussions of law and facts, we have no option but to hold that the Rule has no merit and, as such, the same should be discharged.

13. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the, Rule, thus, stands vacated. The Adalat below is directed to proceed with the execution of the decree in accordance with law.

Communicate this at once.

End.
